mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2% for three consecutive months reduces the present value of future equity cash flows, thereby depressing S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 2% and remains above for 3 months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically lower than during the 30-day pre-trend window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment rates (UNRATE) reduce consumer and business confidence, lowering expected corporate earnings growth and driving negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE crosses above the prior month's value
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not significantly negative relative to the prior 10-day window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in personal consumption expenditures (CPIAUCSL) accompanied by a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) signals a shift from supply-side to demand-driven economic expansion, which tends to boost S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 days.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL monthly growth > 2% while INDPRO monthly growth < -1%
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns show no statistically significant correlation with the combined demand/supply signal (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sustained contraction in industrial production (INDPRO) below 100 for three consecutive months indicates supply-side weakness that dampens investor optimism, producing negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO < 100 for 3 months in a row
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not lower than during the prior supply expansion phase (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the 3-month moving average of FEDFUNDS falls below 1.5%, it suggests policy accommodation, which typically supports equity valuations and yields positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not higher than during the 60-day pre-trend window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in the unemployment rate (UNRATE) below 4% triggers a labor market tightening that often coincides with corporate hiring acceleration and positive S&P 500 forward returns over the next 5 days.
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive relative to the prior 10-day window (t-test p > 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: Concurrent strength in both personal consumption (CPIAUCSL) and retail sales (not in catalog - so use HOUST as proxy for retail) suggests resilient demand, which usually supports equity valuations and produces positive 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL growth > 1% and HOUST > 1000 for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not significantly higher than during periods of single-demand indicator strength (Rank IC < 0.05).

mechanism_narrative: When the combined momentum of all major macro proxies (GDPC1, CPIAUCSL, PAYEMS, RSAFS) forms a positive feedback loop over the next 20 days, it indicates a self-reinforcing economic upcycle that drives S&P 500 forward returns higher.
candidate_trigger: Positive cross-correlation (rho > 0.6) among the four proxies over the prior 10 days
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not higher than expected from the individual proxy trends (multivariate regression p > 0.05).
